title: Tests, Grades and Learning at Home
text:
Many students feel anxious before important exams. Some schools now rely less on final tests and more on continuous assessment, which measures progress across the whole year. Teachers argue that this approach gives a fairer picture of what a student has actually learned. However, critics say that grades based on daily work can be affected by a student's home situation.

Learning at home has become more common, especially since many families began using digital platforms. Parents often help with homework, but they may not always have the time or knowledge to explain difficult topics. As a result, some children fall behind while others make rapid progress. Experts suggest that a regular study routine matters more than the number of hours spent at the desk.

questions.text: According to the passage, what do teachers believe about continuous assessment?
options: It is less stressful than final exams.
It gives a fairer picture of what students have learned.
It is only used in universities.

questions.text: What do experts suggest matters more than the number of hours spent studying?
Why might some children fall behind when they learn at home?
options: Their parents never help them with homework.
Parents may lack the time or knowledge to explain hard topics.
Digital platforms are always too difficult to use.
Teachers stop giving grades during the year.

questions.text: What can be inferred about the critics of continuous assessment?
options: They think grades should ignore daily work.
They believe a student's home situation may affect the grades.
They want to return to final exams because they are cheaper.
They believe students should not be graded at all.

vocabulary.definition: worried and nervous about something that is going to happen
the process of judging someone's work, progress or ability
a regular way of doing things, repeated at set times

paragraph_translations: Muitos alunos se sentem ansiosos antes de provas importantes. Algumas escolas agora dependem menos de provas finais e mais de avaliação contínua, que mede o progresso ao longo de todo o ano. Os professores argumentam que essa abordagem oferece uma visão mais justa do que o aluno realmente aprendeu. No entanto, os críticos dizem que as notas baseadas no trabalho diário podem ser afetadas pela situação familiar do aluno.

A aprendizagem em casa tornou-se mais comum, especialmente desde que muitas famílias começaram a usar plataformas digitais. Os pais frequentemente ajudam com os deveres de casa, mas nem sempre têm tempo ou conhecimento para explicar temas difíceis. Como resultado, algumas crianças ficam para trás enquanto outras progridem rapidamente. Especialistas sugerem que uma rotina de estudos regular importa mais do que o número de horas passadas na escrivaninha.
